claims.text: The overall tribo-corrosion degradation rate of high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by the dynamic balance between protective oxide-film formation and mechanical disruption.
Increasing oxide-forming elements promotes formation of a dense, adherent, potentially spinel-type oxide layer.
A protective surface film retards corrosive attack on the underlying alloy.
A dense oxide film directly reduces mechanical wear.
Rapid mechanical removal or instability of the film produces a wear-corrosion synergy that accelerates total degradation.
AlCoCrFeNiTi or a similar HEA has a multiphase microstructure capable of forming protective oxides under elevated-temperature friction.
The oxide-forming elements Al, Ti, and Cr are uniformly distributed in the proposed initial state.
Higher-temperature sintering can produce a more protective surface film.
Composition or processing can enrich oxide-forming elements at the surface.
Friction and heat generate the protective film by tribo-oxidation.
Under moderate wear, oxide-film regeneration can counteract mechanical film removal.
Maintaining the protective film reduces direct metal dissolution.
Maintaining the protective film reduces material loss from wear.
Corrosion of a depassivated surface can exacerbate subsequent wear.
An alloy engineered for stronger oxide-film formation will have shallower wear tracks than the matched baseline.
An alloy engineered for stronger oxide-film formation will have a lower corrosion current density than the matched baseline.
The engineered alloy will have lower total coupled degradation because both wear and corrosion components are suppressed.
The protective mechanism should operate only when wear intensity, temperature, and oxygen availability permit film reformation.
Under extreme wear or oxygen-deficient conditions, mechanical removal can dominate and the protective mechanism can fail.
The balance between film formation and removal is sensitive to processing, wear intensity, oxygen availability, and temperature.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome describes corrosion current density as measured by both EIS and potentiodynamic polarization, whereas the measurement plan more appropriately associates current density with polarization and passive-film resistance with EIS.
